title: Data-centric benchmark for label noise estimation and ranking in remote sensing Binary building segmentation
mechanism: Rank training images by label noise with an augmented or cross-validated ensemble: noise score = 1 - IoU(prediction, given label), optionally variance-weighted; train on the least-noisy part.
adaptation: Use module-grouped 5-fold roots to get out-of-fold 3-5 seed predictions for all 532 cells; crack noise = 1 - relF1@2 plus missed-component count (tolerant so 1 px jitter does not dominate), inactive noise = 1 - IoU. Do not drop cells (209 crack, 42 inactive): ignore crack loss on worst-ranked cells/components, keep all other classes. First check overlap with the 24 audit-flagged cells.
min_experiment: Arm: house model with crack loss ignored near label segments and on predicted-unlabelled components in worst 10% of cells by OOF crack noise. Baseline: house and PF, 5 seeds. Metric: clean-49 crack relF1@2 and IoU, 5-fold CV crack IoU, F51 AP. Kill: audit-cell overlap no better than random, or < +0.01 relF1@2 on CV and < +0.012 test crack IoU.
evidence: R: Kendall tau 0.61 / Spearman 0.77 vs CleanLab 0.17 / 0.24; U-Net on top-ranked 50% F1 80.34 vs 78.26 on all noisy data (oracle 80.98); boundary shrink/expand noise hardest for all methods. SpaceNet8-derived building set.
prior_overlap: BRIEF Labels row: audit flagged 24/239 cells, nothing fixed; automatic label refinement never run. Open.
